signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish BoJ Repricing
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 107.12, under heavy pressure as JPY leads the G10 board (+0.863% avg across 7 pairs) while AUD lags (-1.057% avg across 4 pairs), establishing an extreme 1.920% bilateral performance spread. BoJ Governor Ueda actively maintained December rate hike expectations overnight, noting that yen weakness threatens higher import costs and food prices. Although RBA's policy rate of 4.85% vs BoJ's 1.25% yields a substantial nominal spread of 360bp in favor of AUD (AONIA vs TONA carry at +362bp), cross-asset risk aversion with VIX elevated at 25.5 and S&P 500 down 1.03% drives rapid carry unwinds. Retail positioning sits at 88% long, running directly against institutional risk-off flows. Options skew reflects defensive positioning with EUR/JPY 25d risk reversals at -1.72 and USD/JPY at -1.71. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY; carry unwind dominates while broader volatility stays elevated. Catalyst: Australia Employment Change at 00:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp risk-on rebound across global equities that stabilizes carry trades above 108.00.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Verbal Intervention Warning + Downside Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 159.33, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (158.33/157.63/158.69) while 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention. Overnight commentary from BoJ Governor Ueda emphasized that soft yen conditions is likely to push up food prices via import costs and kept a December rate hike firmly on the table. Although SOFR at 3.93% vs TONA at 1.23% provides a 270bp carry buffer for the dollar, options markets are heavily pricing downside protection, evidenced by the 1M 25d risk reversal printing at an extreme -1.71 put skew. Implied volatility runs at 7.1% against HV30 of 5.3%, generating a +1.8% volatility risk premium as traders position for policy disruption. JPY speculative positioning sits net short 23,913 contracts (90th percentile of its 52-week range), creating substantial short-covering fuel on any official policy escalation. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; elevated intervention hazard caps upside ahead of 160.00. Catalyst: Japan Core CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: US yields advance and carry demand forces a sustained breakout above 160.50 without official intervention.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD prints at 1.0995, trading below its SMA20 (1.1152), SMA50 (1.1272), and SMA200 (1.1523) in a confirmed downtrend extended 2.39 ATR below its 20-day moving average. Speculative positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short -98,604 contracts at the 6th percentile of the 52-week range (z = -1.58), reflecting crowded institutional selling. Conversely, retail sentiment sits at an extreme 85% long, establishing a stark institutional-versus-retail divergence. Rates favor the greenback, with Fed 4.00% (ON HOLD) vs ECB 2.65% (ON HOLD) generating a 135bp spread favoring USD (SOFR vs €STR at +149bp), while US 5Y yields rose +39bp over 5 sessions (FRED, as of Nov 13), led by a +35bp rise in real yields. Options markets display moderate base put bias with 25d risk reversals at -0.52 and 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.2% vs HV30 of 5.1% (+1.1% VRP). Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; monetary policy divergence and real rate support keep rallies constrained. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y at 10:00 UTC. Risk: Decisive short-covering rally lifting spot above the SMA20 at 1.1152.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Retail Short vs Rate Spread
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4307, printing above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.4092/1.4101/1.3912) in an uptrend that is extended 3.11 ATR above its 20-day average. Retail sentiment has reached an extreme 92% short position, attempting to fade the multi-week rally even as institutional leveraged funds cover shorts (WoW +15,077 contracts). Fundamental support remains solid, as Fed at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.50% provides a 150bp carry premium favoring USD (SOFR vs CORRA at +138bp). Furthermore, Canadian unemployment surprised higher at 6.7% vs 6.3% (z = +3.00σ shock), cementing domestic economic softening relative to resilient US activity. While BEER models flag the pair as rich at z = +1.76σ, retail capitulation risk remains high if price tests fresh highs. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; policy differential and retail contrarian squeeze support the trend. Catalyst: BoC Deputy Governor Gravelle Speech at 22:24 UTC. Risk: Aggressive rebound in crude oil driving spot back below the SMA20 support at 1.4092.
